qe: The Government of India Act, 1935 proposed the formation of an All-India Federation. What was the main condition for this federation to come into existence?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 ने 'अखिल भारतीय महासंघ' के गठन का प्रस्ताव दिया था। इस महासंघ के अस्तित्व में आने के लिए मुख्य शर्त क्या थी?
o: At least 50% of the total population of Indian states had to agree to join
All provinces had to be directly administered by the British Parliament
The Viceroy had to resign from his executive position
The Indian National Congress had to give full administrative control to the princes
e: Detailed Explanation: The federation was conditional on states representing 50% of the total population of Indian states agreeing to join. Since these conditions were never met, the proposed All India Federation never came into existence.

qe: Under the 1935 Act, the subjects at the federal level were divided into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred'. Which subjects were included under 'Reserved'?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत, संघीय स्तर पर विषयों को 'आरक्षित' और 'हस्तांतरित' में विभाजित किया गया था। 'आरक्षित' विषयों के अंतर्गत कौन से विषय शामिल थे?
o: Foreign affairs, defence, tribal areas, and ecclesiastical affairs
Education, health, and local government
Agriculture, industry, and excise
All of the above
e: Detailed Explanation: The 'Reserved' subjects were administered exclusively by the Governor-General on the advice of executive councillors, who were not responsible to the legislature. These included high-stakes areas like defence and foreign affairs.

qe: What was the main difference in the legislative structure between the Council of States and the Federal Assembly under the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत 'काउंसिल ऑफ स्टेट्स' और 'फेडरल असेंबली' के बीच विधायी संरचना में मुख्य अंतर क्या था?
o: Election to the Council of States was direct, while election to the Federal Assembly was indirect
The Federal Assembly was a permanent body while the Council of States had a 5-year term
The Council of States had the power to move a no-confidence motion
All members of both houses were nominated by the British Crown
e: Detailed Explanation: In a departure from typical structures, the 1935 Act mandated that election to the Council of States (Upper House) was direct, whereas election to the Federal Assembly (Lower House) was indirect.

qe: Which of the following was a key feature of the Provincial Autonomy introduced by the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम द्वारा शुरू की गई 'प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता' (Provincial Autonomy) की मुख्य विशेषता क्या थी?
o: Provinces were granted autonomy and a separate legal identity
Provinces were completely abolished
Provinces were placed under the direct control of the District Magistrate
Provinces lost all independent financial powers
e: Detailed Explanation: Provincial autonomy replaced the dyarchy system. Provinces were granted separate legal identities and freed from the superintendence and direction of the Secretary of State and the Governor-General.

qe: How did the 1935 Act affect the voting rights of women?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने महिलाओं के मताधिकार को कैसे प्रभावित किया?
o: Women were given the right to vote on the same basis as men
Women were totally excluded from voting
Women were granted universal adult franchise
Voting rights for women were restricted to the educational elite only
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1935 Act extended the franchise to a wider segment of the population, and women were specifically granted the right to vote on the same basis as men.

qe: What was the official British strategy behind granting provincial autonomy in the 1935 Act regarding the Congress?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम में कांग्रेस के संबंध में प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता देने के पीछे आधिकारिक ब्रिटिश रणनीति क्या थी?
o: To create powerful provincial leaders and provincialise the Congress, thereby weakening central leadership
To grant immediate independence to the Congress
To ban the Congress from participating in provincial elections
To make the Congress the sole governing body of the entire nation
e: Detailed Explanation: The British aimed to weaken the central Congress leadership by fostering powerful provincial leaders who would become autonomous centers of power, effectively 'provincialising' the party.

qe: Why did Jawaharlal Nehru describe the 1935 Act as a 'car, all brakes and no engine'?
qh: जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने 1935 के अधिनियम को 'एक ऐसी कार, जिसमें ब्रेक तो हैं पर इंजन नहीं' क्यों कहा?
o: Because of the numerous 'safeguards' and special powers given to the Governor-General that blocked actual progress
Because the car was manufactured in Britain and was too expensive for Indians
Because the Act lacked any legislative provisions
Because it gave too much power to the Indian Ministers
e: Detailed Explanation: Nehru's famous remark highlighted that while the Act looked grand in structure (the 'car'), the reality was constrained by the Governor-General's extensive powers (the 'brakes'), which prevented any real movement or progress.

qe: Which nationalist organization declared itself in favour of working the 1935 Act at both central and provincial levels?
qh: किस राष्ट्रवादी संगठन ने केंद्र और प्रांतीय स्तरों पर 1935 के अधिनियम को लागू करने (working the act) के पक्ष में घोषणा की?
o: The Hindu Mahasabha and the National Liberal Foundation
The Indian National Congress
The Communist Party of India
The All India Muslim League (initially)
e: Detailed Explanation: While the Congress unanimously rejected the 1935 Act, groups like the Hindu Mahasabha and the National Liberal Foundation expressed their willingness to participate and work within the Act's framework.

qe: Who was the first person to offer individual Satyagraha in 1940?
qh: 1940 में व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह करने वाले पहले व्यक्ति कौन थे?
o: Vinoba Bhave
Jawaharlal Nehru
Vallabhbhai Patel
Maulana Azad
e: Detailed Explanation: Vinoba Bhave was the first person chosen by Mahatma Gandhi to initiate individual satyagraha, followed by Jawaharlal Nehru as the second.

qe: What was the main purpose of the Individual Satyagraha launched by Gandhi in 1940?
qh: 1940 में गांधी द्वारा शुरू किए गए व्यक्तिगत सत्याग्रह का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To express people's feeling that they were not interested in the Second World War
To overthrow the colonial government by force
To merge the Congress with the Indian Army
To declare immediate independence from Britain
e: Detailed Explanation: The Individual Satyagraha was launched to demonstrate that nationalist patience was not weakness and to express the Indian public's disapproval of being dragged into World War II without their consent.

qe: Who did Gandhi designate as his chosen successor just before the Quit India Movement phase?
qh: भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन चरण से ठीक पहले गांधी ने किसे अपना उत्तराधिकारी नामित किया था?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru
Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Rajagopalachari
Subhash Chandra Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite differences in temperament, Gandhi designated Jawaharlal Nehru as his successor, believing Nehru best reflected the inclusive, pluralist idea of India that he championed.

qe: Which mission was sent to India in March 1942 to seek Indian support for the war effort in exchange for constitutional proposals?
qh: मार्च 1942 में युद्ध प्रयासों के लिए भारतीय समर्थन प्राप्त करने के बदले में संवैधानिक प्रस्तावों के साथ भारत किसे भेजा गया था?
o: Cripps Mission
Simon Commission
Cabinet Mission
Lee Commission
e: Detailed Explanation: Stafford Cripps, a member of the British War Cabinet, led a mission to India in March 1942 with a 'draft declaration' to secure Indian cooperation in the ongoing World War II.

qe: What did Mahatma Gandhi call the Cripps Mission proposals after reviewing them?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने क्रिप्स मिशन के प्रस्तावों की समीक्षा करने के बाद उन्हें क्या कहा था?
o: A post-dated cheque
A sunless dawn
A dead letter
A Magna Carta of India
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi famously described the Cripps Mission's offer as a 'post-dated cheque' because the promises of autonomy were for a distant future, with no immediate transfer of real power.

qe: Which of the following was a primary reason for the Congress to reject the Cripps Mission proposals?
qh: कांग्रेस द्वारा क्रिप्स मिशन के प्रस्तावों को अस्वीकार करने का एक मुख्य कारण क्या था?
o: The offer of dominion status instead of complete independence
The offer of immediate full independence
The refusal to divide India into two unions
The demand for the immediate transfer of all military power
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress rejected the proposals because they only offered dominion status rather than complete independence, and the plan allowed provinces to secede, which threatened India's national unity.

qe: Why did the Muslim League reject the Cripps Mission proposals?
qh: मुस्लिम लीग ने क्रिप्स मिशन के प्रस्तावों को क्यों अस्वीकार कर दिया?
o: They felt the proposals denied the Muslims the right to self-determination and the creation of Pakistan
They demanded a merger with the Congress
They wanted to join the British Army
They were satisfied with the status quo
e: Detailed Explanation: The Muslim League criticized the plan because it did not explicitly recognize their demand for the creation of Pakistan, and they felt the machinery for creating a constituent assembly was flawed.

qe: Which of the following was a feature of the 1935 Act regarding the provincial executive?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के संबंध में प्रांतीय कार्यकारी (provincial executive) की एक विशेषता निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी थी?
o: The Governor was to have special powers regarding minorities and law and order
The Governor was to be an elected official
Ministers were to be appointed by the Secretary of State only
Provinces were to be managed by military officers exclusively
e: Detailed Explanation: Under provincial autonomy, the Governor was the Crown's representative but retained special powers to interfere in matters concerning minorities, civil servants, and law and order.

qe: How much of the provincial budget was kept 'non-votable' even under the 1935 Act?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम के तहत भी प्रांतीय बजट का कितना हिस्सा 'गैर-मतदान योग्य' (non-votable) रखा गया था?
o: 40 per cent
80 per cent
10 per cent
50 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite provincial autonomy, the legislature still had limited control over finances, as 40 percent of the provincial budget remained non-votable.

qe: The 1935 Act enfranchised what percentage of the British Indian population?
qh: 1935 के अधिनियम ने ब्रिटिश भारतीय आबादी के कितने प्रतिशत को मताधिकार दिया?
o: 14 per cent
25 per cent
5 per cent
50 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: One of the limitations of the 1935 Act was its narrow franchise, which enfranchised only about 14 percent of the British Indian population.

qe: The 'Delhi Chalo' movement is associated with which satyagraha?
qh: 'दिल्ली चलो' आंदोलन किस सत्याग्रह से संबंधित है?
o: Individual Satyagraha
Salt Satyagraha
Champaran Satyagraha
Quit India Movement
e: Detailed Explanation: In the Individual Satyagraha, after making an anti-war declaration, the satyagrahi would move towards Delhi, leading to it being called the 'Delhi Chalo Movement'.

qe: What was the 'Delhi Manifesto' of 1929 primarily about?
qh: 1929 का 'दिल्ली घोषणापत्र' (Delhi Manifesto) मुख्य रूप से किसके बारे में था?
o: Conditions for attending the Round Table Conference
The formation of the All India Federation
A plan to start the Quit India Movement
An appeal to the British Crown for immediate independence
e: Detailed Explanation: The Delhi Manifesto, issued by nationalist leaders, laid down conditions for participating in the Round Table Conference, primarily that it should aim to draft a constitution for immediate Dominion Status.

qe: Who described the 1935 Act as a 'sunless dawn'?
qh: किसने 1935 के अधिनियम को 'एक सूर्यहीन भोर' (sunless dawn) कहकर वर्णित किया?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Mahatma Gandhi
Jawaharlal Nehru
Subhash Chandra Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: While this phrase was famously applied to the 1919 reforms by Tilak, it captures the general nationalist sentiment toward colonial 'reforms' that provided no real power.

qe: What was the primary motive of the colonial authority for the 'Annulment of the Partition of Bengal' in 1911?
qh: 1911 में 'बंगाल के विभाजन को रद्द करने' के पीछे औपनिवेशिक सत्ता का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To curb the menace of revolutionary terrorism
To please the Indian National Congress
To grant independence to Bengal
To improve the administration of Assam
e: Detailed Explanation: The government decided to annul the partition primarily to appease nationalist sentiment and, more importantly, to curb the rising menace of revolutionary terrorism that had plagued Bengal.

qe: Which of the following was a feature of the 1919 Montagu-Chelmsford reforms regarding the provincial legislature?
qh: प्रांतीय विधायिका के संबंध में 1919 के मोंटेग्यू-चेम्सफोर्ड सुधारों की एक विशेषता निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी थी?
o: Expansion of councils and the elective principle was further consolidated
The legislative councils were abolished
The Governor-General was made a member of the councils
Direct control was given to the Secretary of State
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 reforms expanded provincial legislative councils and established that 70% of the members were to be elected, further consolidating the communal and class-based electorates.

qe: The 1919 Act provided that in the Viceroy's executive council, how many members were to be Indians?
qh: 1919 के अधिनियम में यह प्रावधान था कि वायसराय की कार्यकारी परिषद में कितने सदस्य भारतीय होंगे?
o: Three
One
Five
Half
e: Detailed Explanation: A small but significant change in the central executive was the provision that out of the eight members of the Viceroy’s Executive Council, three were to be Indians.

qe: Who said 'I have not become His Majesty’s first Minister to preside over the liquidation of the British Empire'?
qh: किसने कहा 'मैं महामहिम का पहला मंत्री इसलिए नहीं बना हूँ कि ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य के विघटन की अध्यक्षता करूँ'?
o: Winston Churchill
Ramsay MacDonald
Clement Attlee
Lord Linlithgow
e: Detailed Explanation: This famous quote by Winston Churchill explains the British government's hardline stance against granting India any real independence during World War II.
